page: Microsoft Azure E32pds_v6 is an ARM-based server powered by a Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 3.4 GHz with no hyperthreading. The memory configuration consists of 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, featuring a 1890 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

In benchmark testing, the E32pds_v6 demonstrates strong multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 66297.85 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 20088.0. Memory performance is highly competitive, achieving top-tier results in large-block read-only (449.0 GB/sec) and write (188.31 GB/sec) bandwidth tests, alongside a top-tier PassMark memory score. Database operations are highly efficient, as evidenced by a top-tier PassMark database operations score of 37819.86 and strong Redis SET performance at 61.82 million operations per second. However, large-scale LLM inference is a bottleneck, with 70B model prompt processing scoring in the bottom 10% at 4.65 tokens per second due to the lack of hardware accelerators.

The ARM-based architecture of the Epdsv6 family provides high resource density and memory capacity, offering a cost-effective alternative to traditional x86 memory-optimized instances. This hardware profile is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, relational databases, caching layers like Redis, and web serving applications that benefit from high memory bandwidth and fast local NVMe storage.
description: Microsoft Azure E32pds_v6 is an ARM-based, memory-optimized server powered by a 32-core Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. It features 256.0 GB of RAM (8.0 GB per core) and a bundled 1890 GB NVMe SSD. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance delivers strong multi-core performance and top-tier memory bandwidth, with large-block read-only speeds reaching 449.0 GB/sec. Benchmark results highlight exceptional database capabilities, with a top-tier PassMark database operations score and strong Redis SET throughput. However, the lack of dedicated GPU hardware limits its utility for large-scale LLM inference. The E32pds_v6 is highly cost-effective for memory-intensive applications, relational databases, and high-throughput web serving.
